message.content:
**Answer:** One of the most celebrated sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin (1889)**. It captured the era’s fascination with realism, emotion, and the human form, and it remains an icon of modern sculpture. --- ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin (1840‑1917) | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist; early modernism | | **Material** | Bronze (originally marble) | | **Subject** | A passionate embrace between two lovers | | **Impact** | • Became a symbol of romantic love and artistic freedom.
• Influenced countless artists and became a staple in museums worldwide.
• Its dramatic pose and textured surface exemplified Rodin’s break from classical idealism. | --- ### Other notable 19th‑century sculptures | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Significance | |-----------|--------|------|--------------| | **The Gates of Hell** | Rodin | 1880‑1917 | A monumental series of figures inspired by Dante’s *Inferno*. | | **The Thinker** | Rodin | 1902‑03 (early 20th) | Though technically early 20th, its conception began in the late 19th and it remains the most iconic of Rodin’s works. | | **The Statue of Liberty** | Frédéric Baron Houdon (design) & Alexandre Gros (sculpture) | 1886 | A monumental gift from France to the U.S., embodying liberty and enlightenment. | | **The Venus de Milo** | Unknown (ancient) | Reintroduced in the 19th‑century museum context, it revived interest in classical sculpture. | --- ### Bottom line While many masterpieces were produced in the 19th century, **“The Kiss” by Rodin** is often cited as the most famous sculpture of that period due to its widespread influence, iconic status, and enduring presence in art history.
